title: Print a number
description: Use print() to show any number you choose. For example, print(100) or print(25).
hints: Write print() in the code area.
Put any number inside the brackets, for example print(100).
Run your code. Any number printed with print() is accepted.
explanation: Use print() to display a number on the screen. You can choose 100, 25, 7, or any other number.
commonMistakes: Make sure you write print, add opening and closing brackets, and put a number inside them.

validation.feedback: Use print(...) to display any number you choose.

title: Print a character
description: Use print() to show one character on the screen. For example, print("A") or print("#"). You can choose any character.
hints: Write print() in the code area.
Put one character inside quotation marks and brackets.
Run your code. Any single character printed with print() is accepted.
explanation: A character can be a letter, number, or symbol. Use print() to show the character you choose.
commonMistakes: Write print with brackets and put the character inside single or double quotation marks.

validation.feedback: Use print(...) to display one character.

title: Print two messages on two lines
description: Use print() on two separate lines. Write one message in each print() statement.
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Your program should display at least two non-empty lines.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: This task gives you practice with print two lines. The reference solution is only one example; other working approaches are accepted when they use the required Python feature.
commonMistakes: Check brackets and quotes, use the correct indentation, and make sure you actually use the Python feature asked for in the task.

validation.feedback: Your program should display at least two non-empty lines.

description: Use print() to show the answer to 8 + 5. You can also try adding two different numbers.
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Use + in a calculation and display the numeric result.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: This task gives you practice with print a calculation. The reference solution is only one example; other working approaches are accepted when they use the required Python feature.
commonMistakes: Check brackets and quotes, use the correct indentation, and make sure you actually use the Python feature asked for in the task.

validation.feedback: Use + in a calculation and display the numeric result.
